response.sql: WITH per_order AS (SELECT orderslink, AVG(feerate - rebrate) AS avg_net, AVG(rebtotal) AS avg_reb FROM fees GROUP BY orderslink), overall AS (SELECT AVG(feerate - rebrate) AS overall_net FROM fees) SELECT AVG(p.avg_reb) AS mean_avg_rebtotal, AVG(p.avg_net) AS mean_avg_net_fee_rate, AVG(p.avg_net - o.overall_net) AS mean_excess FROM per_order p CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE p.avg_net > o.overall_net

assumptions.assumption: The overall average net fee rate is the average of (feerate - rebrate) across all individual fee rows. Rows where feerate or rebrate is NULL are skipped.
Fee rows with NULL orderslink form a single group, which GROUP BY does naturally. Groups whose average net rate is NULL are excluded by the comparison.
The average total rebate per order skips NULL rebtotal values. Nothing is rounded.

alternatives.interpretation: The overall average net fee rate is the mean of the per-order (group) average net rates, so each order counts equally, rather than the row-level average.
